item.title: Back Bay Farm
item.description:
A working farm along Back Bay growing seasonal vegetables and keeping a small flock of pasture-raised laying hens. Produce goes straight from the field to the Saturday farm stand or into weekly subscription boxes.

Farm boxes are available weekly or biweekly, sized for a family of two to four, and can be picked up at the farm or a Town Center drop point.

item.title: Chesapeake Cellars
item.description:
A family-run cellar producing a few thousand cases a year from Virginia-grown grapes. The tasting room pours flights of five, with a rotating selection tied to what just came out of the barrel.

Weekend tastings are walk-in, and the cellar hosts a handful of private events each year for groups of up to twenty.

item.title: Lynnhaven Woodworks
item.description:
A one-shop woodworking studio building solid hardwood furniture the old way: joined, not glued together from panels. Most hardwood comes from downed trees within an hour of the shop.

Specializes in dining tables and built-in cabinetry, with a typical lead time of six to eight weeks for a custom piece.

item.title: Oceanfront Leather Co.
item.description:
Full-grain leather, hand-cut and saddle-stitched, no machine shortcuts. Every bag and wallet is built to be repaired, not replaced, and comes with a lifetime stitching guarantee.

A small storefront in Norfolk doubles as the workshop, so what you see being made is usually what’s on the shelf.

item.title: Private Concierge Services — 757 Local Trading Co.
Salt Marsh Photography
item.description:
A one-photographer studio shooting weddings, portraits and product photography for small businesses across Hampton Roads, with a particular eye for waterfront light.

Wedding season books up early, but weekday sessions for headshots, product photography and small-business branding are usually available with a week or two of notice.

item.title: Tidewater Ceramics
item.description:
Every piece starts on the wheel in a small studio a few blocks from the Oceanfront. Stoneware is fired twice, glazed by hand, and finished in batches small enough that no two plates are quite the same.

Best known for a warm, sand-toned dinnerware line carried by a handful of restaurants across Hampton Roads, and for taking on custom commissions for weddings and housewarmings.
